finding: The site has no live range for this job, so there is nothing to grade. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $157-$335; midsize 2016 Camry about $169-$370; truck 2016 F-150 5.0L about $160-$360; luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $229-$490, before any battery registration. These sit close to the benchmarks: Jerry gives $268-$368 installed, a battery chain gives $185-$400 for the battery with installation often free, a mobile mechanic chain's figures add up to about $100-$370, and RepairPal shows $223-$251 for a 2021 Honda Civic. Candidly, this is a menu-priced service: the battery chain whose guide was loaded says most of its locations fit a battery free with purchase and otherwise charge $20-$75, so a real bill can be just the battery price plus tax and core, which is at or below the bottom of a parts-plus-book-time build; the top of each built range (a full hour at $160) is what a repair shop or dealer billing normal labor might reach, not what most drivers pay. Second look on 2026-11-20, what changed: (1) the Toyota high ends are now genuine list prices from an online Toyota OEM catalog, TrueStart 00544-35060-550 at $174.71 for the Corolla and 00544-24F60-575 at $209.97 for the Camry (a Toyota dealer site shows $205.93 for the same Camry battery), replacing the retailer's top tier; the Camry's size 24F is now confirmed by that catalog's fitment. The catalog marks both as currently unavailable to order, and its Corolla fitment row does not break out years. (2) Two maker-stated times for swapping the 12-volt battery alone were found, both warranty times for other vehicles: GM's 0.3 hr add-on for the Chevrolet Bolt (now the economy low) and FCA's 0.4 hr 'Battery - Replace' for the 2017 Dodge Charger and Chrysler 300 (now the midsize low). How solid the hours are: still weak. No class has a time stated for its own example vehicle; Toyota, Ford and BMW print none that could be found. The truck and luxury low ends and every high end still rest on one general guide's 20-60 minutes. Other maker times found cover more than the swap and are cross-checks only: Subaru 0.5 hr test and replace (0.2 hr for the test alone), Ram 1500 diesel 0.3 hr inspect and replace, Jeep Wrangler 0.5 hr test, charge, retest and replace, Honda CR-V 0.7 hr with a software update. Together they say a dealer's warranty time for this job is about 0.3-0.5 hr, which fits inside the range used. Parts: the Ford and BMW high ends are genuine list prices from OEM catalogs, and the BMW's exact battery size was not confirmed from a loaded source. The low ends use a national retailer's mid tier ($120.51); its budget tier is $81.37. BMW battery registration: no source stating a time or price was found, so it is not included and the luxury total could be higher. Reviewer note 2026-11-20: the economy low end stays at 0.33 hr (general guide); the GM 0.3 hr add-on time for a Bolt EV agrees with it but is a cross-check only, so the economy build is about $160-$335. Posted prices (added 2026-11-20): seven sellers' own pages, two national chains and five car dealers in five states, print a battery at $134.95 to $389.95: the chains' battery-only prices start at $134.95-$311.99 with fitting free on a current offer or worth up to $19.99-$35, and dealers post $162.51-$389.95 installed (AGM at the top), which matches the built ranges and confirms that fitting is a small or zero charge rather than an hour of labor; Walmart and Advance Auto Parts state free installation with purchase but the pages loaded showed no battery price, and no independent shop's posted price was found.
extras: A quote often adds a refundable core charge until the old battery is handed back (none of the pages loaded stated the amount, and it is left out of the prices here), a battery and charging system test, terminal cleaning or anti-corrosion treatment, shop supplies or a battery disposal fee, and sales tax. Some cars, BMW among them, need the new battery registered or coded to the car's computer, which a shop may charge for separately; no stated time or price for that was found. On some vehicles the battery sits under a seat, in the trunk or behind a wheel-well liner, which takes longer than the general times used here. A weak battery can also be a sign of a charging fault, so an alternator test may be suggested.
